description: Classical South Indian Vastu text attributed to sage Maya, outlining the technical rules of site orientation, padavinyasa grid planning, and structural proportioning for residential temples and houses.
schools_note: Followed extensively in Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and parts of Karnataka and coastal Maharashtra. Emphasizes strict calculation of Ayadi Shadvarga (gain, loss, nakshatra, yoni).

rules.rationale: Structures must strictly align to cardinal axes established by gnomon (shanku) shadow casting, avoiding skew/diagonal corner orientations.
rules.source: Mayamatam, Ch. 6 (Gnomon and Cardinal Orientation), Verses 1-15

rules.rationale: Agneya (South-East) is assigned to Agni; cooking hearth placed here preserves domestic peace and health.
Nairutya (South-West) represents the Pitrus (ancestors) and steady earth; ensures uninterrupted leadership.
Varuna (West) and Ishana (North-East) govern bodies of water, well digging, and rainwater cisterns.
Kubera (North) governs wealth and grain reservoirs; dry storage in northern quadrants maintains longevity.
The central quadrant (Brahma) must be immaculate; columns intersecting the central marma points bring ruin.
Ishana corner is dedicated to Shiva/Supreme consciousness for ritual consecration.
Disposal of bodily refuse must be confined to the wind (Vayu) or Yama quadrants, never facing sunrise.
Deep shaded verandah (alimpanam) along the east and north buffers tropical heat and welcomes guests.
Flights of steps (sopana) must rise from West to East or South to North, occupying the dense southern flank.
